deals.evidence: 5% of Monumental at that $4.05 billion valuation.
deals.headline: QIA buys 5% of Monumental Sports & Entertainment
deals.summary: Qatar's sovereign wealth fund bought a 5% passive minority stake in Monumental (Capitals, Wizards, Mystics, Capital One Arena, Monumental Sports Network) at a $4.05 billion valuation, the first sovereign fund to invest directly in a major US team.

deals.evidence: Laurene Powell Jobs, who previously sold some of her holdings to another Monumental limited partner, is now out of the company entirely.
deals.headline: Powell Jobs sells part of her Monumental stake
deals.summary: Laurene Powell Jobs, who bought roughly 20% of Monumental in 2017, began selling about half her holding in 2024 and sold some of it to another Monumental limited partner; buyer, stake and price not stated.

deals.evidence: announced Arctos Partners ("Arctos"), as the organization's newest minority investor
deals.headline: Arctos becomes a minority investor in Monumental Sports & Entertainment
deals.summary: Arctos bought a passive minority stake in Monumental from Laurene Powell Jobs at a $7.2 billion enterprise value, with no board seats; stake and price not disclosed.

deals.evidence: The deals give Monumental an enterprise value of $7.2 billion
deals.headline: QIA increases its stake in Monumental Sports & Entertainment
deals.summary: QIA increased its equity stake alongside Arctos's entry, buying equity previously held by Laurene Powell Jobs at a $7.2 billion enterprise value; new percentage not disclosed.

deals.evidence: The District of Columbia Government will provide $515 million toward the catalytic project
deals.headline: DC commits $515M to ~$800M Capital One Arena transformation
deals.investor: Government of the District of Columbia
deals.summary: The District provides $515 million toward an approximately $800 million renovation (including $87.5 million to buy the arena, which Monumental leases back through 2050); Monumental contributes at least $285 million plus the sale proceeds and carries overruns. The Capitals and Wizards stay through 2050.

name: Washington Capitals
notes: Revenue, operating income (EBITDA) and player expenses are Forbes estimates for 2024-25 (USD, net of revenue sharing and arena debt service); valuation is Forbes enterprise value of the Capitals alone, calculated December 2025 (Forbes: owner Ted Leonsis, purchased 1999 for $85M; the $85M is on the Forbes page as '$85M'). Monumental-level deals value the whole company (Capitals, Wizards, Mystics, arena, network): $4.05bn (June 2023) and $7.2bn enterprise value (Dec 2025). QIA's stake was 5% from 2023 and was increased in Dec 2025 (new % not stated), so its owner row carries stake null; Leonsis's percentage is not stated. Legal entity 'Lincoln Hockey' is from the copyright line on the team's NHL.com staff page (dated 1999-2020). Stadium owner and $87.5M sale-leaseback are from Monumental's October 21, 2024 release (monumentalsports.com blocks automated reads; read via fetch); capitalonearena.com says Leonsis became majority owner of the arena in June 2010. Missing: arena capacity, honours (2018 Stanley Cup not read on a citable page), social, attendance, sponsors.
